title: Machine-learning prioritization informed preclinical study of luteolin in heart-failure models
summary: Machine-learning analysis prioritized a candidate gene signature for investigation of luteolin in cell and rat heart-failure models. The study reports changes in cardiac injury measures alongside the signature. This is preclinical evidence without independent clinical validation and does not establish treatment efficacy in people.
ai_technology: Machine-learning combinations prioritized a gene signature from bioinformatic target sets for experimental follow-up.
organization: The First College of Clinical Medicine, Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine, Nanning, China

evidence.tested: Cell and rat models were used for experimental follow-up of the learned signature and proposed pathway; no independent clinical cohort was tested.
evidence.unknown: Preclinical models do not establish efficacy in people; authors note absent gene-editing validation.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning combinations prioritized a gene signature from bioinformatic target sets for experimental follow-up.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
